claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure with approximately 2 μm interlamellar spacing.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Severe plastic deformation followed by an isothermal hold will transform the continuous lamellar structure into discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix.
A treatment temperature of 600–800 °C, followed by a 1–4 hour hold slightly below the B2 ordering transition, is an effective phase-inversion window.
Hydrostatic pressure above 1 GPa during deformation suppresses void nucleation.
A strain rate above 10^-2 s^-1 generates the high dislocation density required for the treatment.
Limiting the isothermal hold to 1–4 hours prevents Ostwald ripening.
Severe deformation introduces defects and stored energy that lower the kinetic barrier for phase inversion.
The subsequent thermal hold causes the B2 phase to coalesce into discrete particles rather than retain a continuous lamellar network.
Continuous ordered B2 pathways promote poor ductility and act as crack-propagation channels.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix facilitates dislocation glide and strain hardening.

In refractory high-entropy alloys, an inverted microstructure consisting of discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix improves room-temperature compressive ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
Rounded B2 precipitates mitigate stress concentration at phase interfaces.
The treatment will raise room-temperature tensile fracture strain above 10%.
Discrete B2 precipitation will maintain high yield strength after the treatment.
Exceeding the upper treatment-temperature limit will cause excessive coarsening or phase dissolution.
Insufficient pressure or strain will fail to break the continuity of the lamellar structure.
Phase stability and B2-ordering kinetics in this alloy are highly sensitive to composition, including the Al/Ni ratio.
Conventional HIP at 1200 °C and 207 MPa for 1 hour is an appropriate control for isolating the effect of extreme pressure and deformation.

contradictions.description: The starting lamellae are alternately identified as B2/BCC and FCC/B2. The proposed product and XRD plan assume a continuous BCC matrix and B2/BCC ratios, but no explicit FCC-to-BCC transformation is stated or supported.
